question_text: What are the most common causes of bacterial spoilage in wine? What effect do they each have, and what measures can be employed to guard against them? Your answer may consider the whole grape growing and winemaking process.
command_word: What are the most common causes … What effect do they each have … what measures can be employed
command_word_demand: A three-part enumeration that had to name the actual bacterial spoilage organisms and cover roughly half the ground on each: "Acetobacter and LAB were the main issues to be covered here but several candidates failed to mention LAB and thus could not gain good marks if ignoring approximately half the required coverage."

definitions_required.quote: A definition of "spoilage" would have been useful here as too many talked about general microbial issues in the vineyards and wasted time rather than focusing on the negative effect on the wine itself.

required_elements.element: Cover both Acetobacter and lactic acid bacteria (LAB) — omitting LAB forfeits roughly half the marks
required_elements.quote: Acetobacter and LAB were the main issues to be covered here but several candidates failed to mention LAB and thus could not gain good marks if ignoring approximately half the required coverage.

required_elements.element: Confine the answer to bacteria — demonstrate the distinction between bacteria and fungi/yeast
required_elements.quote: However far too many candidates seemed unaware of the difference between bacteria and fungi (different kingdoms of life!) and wasted time talking about Brettanomyces and yeast.

required_elements.element: Supply technical and numerical detail rather than qualitative description
required_elements.quote: Some technical and numerical detail was essential here to gain good marks.

required_elements.element: Focus on the negative effect on the wine itself, not general vineyard microbiology
required_elements.quote: too many talked about general microbial issues in the vineyards and wasted time rather than focusing on the negative effect on the wine itself

credit_signals.signal: The question was fully answerable to a high standard — top scripts reached the high 70s
credit_signals.quote: A very varied standard of answers with marks ranging from 20s to high 70s. This showed that the question could be answered well.

credit_signals.signal: Cite actual technical values rather than vague comparatives (paper-level expectation for Paper 3)
credit_signals.quote: Vague comments like "lower levels of SO2" are not sufficient - actual numbers are required.

penalty_signals.signal: Spent time on Brettanomyces and yeast, which are not bacteria
penalty_signals.quote: far too many candidates seemed unaware of the difference between bacteria and fungi (different kingdoms of life!) and wasted time talking about Brettanomyces and yeast

penalty_signals.signal: Classified TCA, reduction, mildew or botrytis as bacterial problems
penalty_signals.quote: Some even believed that TCA, reduction, mildew and botrytis were bacterial issues.

penalty_signals.signal: Failed to mention LAB at all
penalty_signals.quote: several candidates failed to mention LAB and thus could not gain good marks if ignoring approximately half the required coverage

penalty_signals.signal: Sloppy chemical terminology and unsense-checked numbers (paper-level)
penalty_signals.quote: Inaccurate use of "Sulphur" instead of sulphites or sulphur dioxide still crops up regularly. Candidates need to allow time to do a sense check on numbers stated too - 50mg of molecular SO2 or SO2 in grammes per litre both undermine Examiners' confidence in a candidate's understanding.

examples_expected.specificity: Actual technical numbers — EU SO2 limits, typical free SO2 levels, real pH values, additive usage levels, filtration pore sizes — not vague comparatives
examples_expected.quote: Paper 3 is a technical paper and it is expected that candidates will have a firm grasp of some key technical information. EU limits for SO2 use, typical levels of free SO2, actual values for pH, permitted and actual usage levels for other additives, pore sizes for filtration and so on are key knowledge for MWs.

scope_traps.trap: Reading "bacterial spoilage" as any microbial fault, and so writing about Brett, TCA, reduction, mildew or botrytis
scope_traps.quote: Some even believed that TCA, reduction, mildew and botrytis were bacterial issues.

scope_traps.trap: Taking the "whole grape growing and winemaking process" licence as an invitation to survey vineyard microbiology generally
scope_traps.quote: too many talked about general microbial issues in the vineyards and wasted time rather than focusing on the negative effect on the wine itself

performance_note: "A very varied standard of answers with marks ranging from 20s to high 70s."
extraction_notes: The examples/technical-numbers requirement and the terminology penalty are drawn from the Panel Chair's paper-level General Comments for Paper 3, not from this question's own commentary; the question-specific commentary states only that "Some technical and numerical detail was essential here". Paper 3 has no Section A/B split, so section is null.

question_text: What should a winemaker's main considerations be when preparing a finished wine for bottling?
command_word: What should a winemaker's main considerations be
command_word_demand: Breadth across the whole set of pre-bottling considerations rather than depth on one: "This was quite a broad question so it was important that candidate did show adequate breadth of knowledge. Many candidates simply failed to cover enough ground".

required_elements.element: Cover wine stability AND legal conformity AND chemical analysis — not just one of the three
required_elements.quote: the answer needed to cover … wine stability but also legal conformity and chemical analysis, and many answers only did part of this

required_elements.element: Know the legal limits for SO2
required_elements.quote: SO2 was generally well covered (though not knowing legal limits is disappointing in an MW candidate)

required_elements.element: Show understanding of additives beyond SO2
required_elements.quote: understanding of the use of other additives was less good

required_elements.element: Keep the answer on the wine itself — the thinking behind preparing the finished wine
required_elements.quote: The question was on preparing a finished wine for bottling, rather than preparing the bottling line: some candidates focused on line hygiene or packaging and didn't expand on the thinking around the wine.

credit_signals.signal: Practical coverage supported by examples scored well here; deep technical theory was not the discriminator
credit_signals.quote: This question provided the highest pass rate on this paper, perhaps because it could be answered well by covering practical aspects and using examples rather than having to show high levels of technical understanding.

credit_signals.signal: Define the question at the outset and stay on it
credit_signals.quote: Here again candidates could usefully focus on defining the question and sticking to the topic as asked.

penalty_signals.signal: Covered too little ground for a deliberately broad question
penalty_signals.quote: Many candidates simply failed to cover enough ground

penalty_signals.signal: Wrote about bottling-line hygiene or packaging instead of the wine
penalty_signals.quote: some candidates focused on line hygiene or packaging and didn't expand on the thinking around the wine

penalty_signals.signal: Did not know the legal SO2 limits
penalty_signals.quote: though not knowing legal limits is disappointing in an MW candidate

examples_expected.specificity: Practical, real-world examples of pre-bottling practice; Paper 3 additionally expects actual technical values (EU SO2 limits, free SO2 levels, additive usage levels) rather than vague comparatives
examples_expected.quote: it could be answered well by covering practical aspects and using examples rather than having to show high levels of technical understanding

scope_traps.trap: Reading "preparing … for bottling" as preparing the bottling line (hygiene, packaging) rather than preparing the wine
scope_traps.quote: The question was on preparing a finished wine for bottling, rather than preparing the bottling line: some candidates focused on line hygiene or packaging and didn't expand on the thinking around the wine.

performance_note: "This question provided the highest pass rate on this paper".
extraction_notes: The required-elements quote is trimmed with … to drop an OCR-intruded page number: the raw commentary reads "the answer needed to cover 15 wine stability but also legal conformity and chemical analysis". The technical-numbers half of examples_expected.specificity comes from the Paper 3 paper-level General Comments, not this question's commentary. Paper 3 has no Section A/B split, so section is null.

question_text: Consider the key issues for storage of wine after packing is complete.
command_word_demand: "Consider" demanded discussion in depth, not assertion: "A considerable number merely made statements without getting into any depth of discussion or detail to show to the Examiner that they understood not just the question but also the key point that they were making."

required_elements.element: Develop each point in depth — show the Examiner you understand the point you are making, not just that you can state it
required_elements.quote: A considerable number merely made statements without getting into any depth of discussion or detail to show to the Examiner that they understood not just the question but also the key point that they were making.

required_elements.element: Stay on post-packaging storage; do not drift into adjacent topics
required_elements.quote: Many of the candidates went off on a tangent and focused on areas not relevant to the question - transport was a common distraction.

required_elements.element: Support the argument with real evidence/examples, hard though they are to find for this topic
required_elements.quote: In an essay like this it was perhaps not easy to find examples and this proved to be the case with many candidates not providing sufficient real evidence to support their point of view.

required_elements.element: Be succinct
required_elements.quote: As a result, a number of the essays rambled when they needed to be more succinct.

credit_signals.signal: The question was scoreable to a high level despite the low pass rate
credit_signals.quote: This question had the lowest pass mark of this paper but some candidates scored over 70% so it certainly wasn't impossible!

penalty_signals.signal: Drifted onto transport rather than storage
penalty_signals.quote: transport was a common distraction

penalty_signals.signal: Made bare statements with no depth of discussion or detail
penalty_signals.quote: A considerable number merely made statements without getting into any depth of discussion or detail

penalty_signals.signal: Rambled
penalty_signals.quote: a number of the essays rambled when they needed to be more succinct

penalty_signals.signal: Offered opinions without real evidence
penalty_signals.quote: many candidates not providing sufficient real evidence to support their point of view

examples_expected.specificity: Real evidence supporting each point of view; the examiners acknowledge examples are hard to find for this topic but still expected them
examples_expected.quote: In an essay like this it was perhaps not easy to find examples and this proved to be the case with many candidates not providing sufficient real evidence to support their point of view.

scope_traps.trap: Treating "storage after packing is complete" as including transport/logistics
scope_traps.quote: Many of the candidates went off on a tangent and focused on areas not relevant to the question - transport was a common distraction.

performance_note: "This question had the lowest pass mark of this paper but some candidates scored over 70% so it certainly wasn't impossible!"
extraction_notes: evidence_quality set to thin despite a full paragraph of commentary because the commentary is entirely about approach (depth, focus, succinctness, evidence) and names NO substantive content that a good answer needed to contain — no storage variable, no threshold, no fault. A grader must not infer topic coverage from this rubric. Paper 3 has no Section A/B split, so section is null.

question_text:
Evaluate the prevention and correction of the following problems:

a. Pinking in a white wine made for drinking early
b. Phenolic bitterness in a red wine
c. High levels of volatile acidity in a full bodied red wine
command_word_demand: Technical accuracy across all three named problems, concisely: "candidates did need to understand all three parts of the question to gain high marks, though answers could be quite concise"; "Technical accuracy is a requirement on this type of question and this let several candidates down."

required_elements.element: Answer all three parts (pinking, phenolic bitterness, high VA) — partial coverage caps the mark
required_elements.quote: Unfortunately, that meant candidates did need to understand all three parts of the question to gain high marks, though answers could be quite concise.

required_elements.element: Get the mechanism of pinking right — it is not caused by oxidative handling
required_elements.quote: Pinking was clearly the least well understood of the three topics, and was the primary reason for many candidates failing to gain a pass mark on this question. Many thought the phenomenon is due to oxidative handling in winemaking, when it's actually the reverse.

required_elements.element: Technical accuracy throughout
required_elements.quote: Technical accuracy is a requirement on this type of question and this let several candidates down.

credit_signals.signal: Concision was acceptable — breadth across the three parts mattered more than length on any one
credit_signals.quote: candidates did need to understand all three parts of the question to gain high marks, though answers could be quite concise

penalty_signals.signal: Attributed pinking to oxidative handling (the reverse of the true cause)
penalty_signals.quote: Many thought the phenomenon is due to oxidative handling in winemaking, when it's actually the reverse.

penalty_signals.signal: Technical inaccuracy
penalty_signals.quote: Technical accuracy is a requirement on this type of question and this let several candidates down.

performance_note: "Perhaps this was why it was the least popular question."
extraction_notes: The commentary says nothing about examples for this question, so examples_expected.required is False; note however that the Paper 3 paper-level General Comments demand actual technical numbers throughout the paper ("Vague comments like \"lower levels of SO2\" are not sufficient - actual numbers are required."), which a grader may reasonably apply to the technical detail here. The report does not state what the correct mechanism of pinking IS — only that oxidative handling is the wrong answer — so the rubric deliberately does not assert one. Paper 3 has no Section A/B split, so section is null.

question_text: Who is making money in the wine industry and why? Discuss in detail three specific examples of profitable wine businesses from different parts of the wine industry supply chain.
command_word_demand: "Discuss in detail" meant quantified insight into each business, not description: "Examiners were looking for high quality insight into businesses in the different parts of the supply chain… We needed numbers, profit, margins, ROI, not theory or a list of companies that have been perceived to be profitable."

required_elements.element: Three specific businesses drawn from DIFFERENT parts of the supply chain — the question itself sets the structure
required_elements.quote: With a question that, to a large extent, defined the structure of the answer, Examiners were looking for high quality insight into businesses in the different parts of the supply chain.

required_elements.element: Quantify profitability — numbers, profit, margins, ROI
required_elements.quote: We needed numbers, profit, margins, ROI, not theory or a list of companies that have been perceived to be profitable.

required_elements.element: Factual accuracy of the examples used — the Examiners check them
required_elements.quote: One thing to bear in mind is that examples need to be accurate as such a factual and empirical paper can be checked for accuracy!

required_elements.element: Keep it succinct and protect time management across the three questions
required_elements.quote: Perhaps the biggest challenge lay in keeping this succinct - a number of candidates failed this question (and probably suffered in time management as a result).

credit_signals.signal: High-quality insight into how each business actually makes money was the whole discriminator
credit_signals.quote: Simply put, those who could demonstrate that insight did well, those that couldn't didn't.

penalty_signals.signal: Gave theory, or a list of companies assumed to be profitable, instead of financial evidence
penalty_signals.quote: not theory or a list of companies that have been perceived to be profitable

penalty_signals.signal: Wrote at excessive length, damaging this answer and the rest of the paper
penalty_signals.quote: Perhaps the biggest challenge lay in keeping this succinct - a number of candidates failed this question (and probably suffered in time management as a result).

penalty_signals.signal: Used inaccurate examples
penalty_signals.quote: examples need to be accurate as such a factual and empirical paper can be checked for accuracy

examples_expected.specificity: Three named, accurate, profitable businesses from different points of the supply chain, each backed by numbers, profit, margins and ROI
examples_expected.quote: We needed numbers, profit, margins, ROI, not theory or a list of companies that have been perceived to be profitable.

performance_note: "This question was attempted by the majority of candidates."
extraction_notes: The report names no specific businesses, so named_in_report is empty by design — do not let a grader expect particular companies.

question_text: There is much talk of consolidation in the wine industry, but where is the industry fragmenting and why? Give examples of businesses that are succeeding as a result.
command_word: where is the industry fragmenting and why? Give examples
command_word_demand: The "why" carried the marks; examples alone did not answer it: "there was a sense that this became of list of smaller companies doing well, with not enough exploration of why."

required_elements.element: Explain WHY fragmentation is occurring in the areas identified — not merely name businesses doing well
required_elements.quote: Mostly, though, there was a sense that this became of list of smaller companies doing well, with not enough exploration of why.

required_elements.element: Draw examples from around the world rather than one market
required_elements.quote: This was also a question whereby a set of global answers added a great deal to the credibility to the candidate's response.

required_elements.element: Plan the answer before writing — this was an unfamiliar framing
required_elements.quote: it was somewhat out of the ordinary and would have required some careful initial thinking before committing to paper

credit_signals.signal: Ability to reason from first principles on an unusual question under time pressure
credit_signals.quote: This question really tested the candidate's ability to think on their feet under time constraint and there were a small handful of excellent answers.

credit_signals.signal: Global spread of examples added credibility
credit_signals.quote: a set of global answers added a great deal to the credibility to the candidate's response

penalty_signals.signal: Produced a list of small successful companies without explaining the causes of fragmentation
penalty_signals.quote: this became of list of smaller companies doing well, with not enough exploration of why

penalty_signals.signal: Answers unsupported by data (paper-level)
penalty_signals.quote: The other major concern is the lack of data and empirical evidence to support arguments. There were many answers with no factual evidence; this is a commercial paper and it is simply not possible to answer successfully without detailed analysis and real life examples.

examples_expected.specificity: Businesses succeeding as a result of fragmentation, drawn globally rather than from a single market, each tied back to WHY that part of the industry is fragmenting
examples_expected.quote: This was also a question whereby a set of global answers added a great deal to the credibility to the candidate's response.

performance_note: "Only 17 candidates attempted this question"; "there were a small handful of excellent answers."
extraction_notes: The second penalty signal is from the Panel Chair's Paper 4 paper-level General Comments, not this question's commentary. The commentary quote "this became of list of smaller companies" is verbatim (sic) from the report.

question_text: What is a "virtual winery"? Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of this business model.
command_word_demand: A straightforward pros-and-cons discussion across three specified angles: "This is purely about understanding the pros and cons, both from a financial and marketing/brand building perspective as well as the pragmatics."

required_elements.element: Cover strengths and weaknesses from a financial perspective, a marketing/brand-building perspective, and the practical pragmatics
required_elements.quote: This is purely about understanding the pros and cons, both from a financial and marketing/brand building perspective as well as the pragmatics.

required_elements.element: Set the model in its current commercial context, including consumer demand for provenance and authenticity
required_elements.quote: Clearly this is an … increasing type of business model, and becoming more and more relevant, despite growing consumer demand for provenance and product authenticity.

required_elements.element: Bring first-hand examples of virtual wineries
required_elements.quote: Having good, personal examples is a massive help.

credit_signals.quote: Having good, personal examples is a massive help.

credit_signals.signal: The structure was not the challenge — depth and context were
credit_signals.quote: The strengths and weaknesses are fairly standard, and structurally this is not a challenging question; hence the high pass rate.

penalty_signals.signal: Superficial treatment with no commercial context
penalty_signals.quote: Poorer answers were too superficial and lacked context.

examples_expected.specificity: Good, personal (first-hand) examples of virtual wine businesses
examples_expected.quote: Having good, personal examples is a massive help.

performance_note: "An uncomplicated question, but not very popular with only 21 responses. Those that did answer were generally successful, with the highest pass rate at approaching 60%."
extraction_notes: The question opens "What is a 'virtual winery'?", which implies a definition is needed, but the report never comments on defining the term — definitions_required is therefore left empty rather than inferred. One quote is trimmed with … to drop an OCR-intruded page number ("this is an 17 increasing type of business model").

question_text: What are the most quantifiable signs that a wine brand is strong?
command_word: What are the most quantifiable signs
command_word_demand: "Quantifiable" was the load-bearing word and defined the whole answer: "There were really very few excellent answers here and no doubt the key word was "quantifiable". This surely points towards the metrics/measurable elements of brand evaluation."

required_elements.element: Answer in metrics — the measurable elements of brand evaluation
required_elements.quote: no doubt the key word was "quantifiable". This surely points towards the metrics/measurable elements of brand evaluation.

required_elements.element: Impose your own structure on an open question and hold it to the end
required_elements.quote: This needed the candidates to apply their own structure, and this is where a lot fell short. The Examiners' comments are littered with "lack of structure", "wandering", "starts well then meanders".

credit_signals.signal: Knowledge of what brand owners and their marketing teams actually measure to track brand progress
credit_signals.quote: Candidates should seek out brand owners and ask what they measure to gauge the progress of their brands and the marketing teams of those brand owners to see what they look for on a Monday morning.

penalty_signals.signal: Listed strong brands instead of the metrics that show strength
penalty_signals.quote: All too often this just became a list of strong brands - not at all what the question was looking for.

penalty_signals.signal: Unstructured, wandering answers
penalty_signals.quote: The Examiners' comments are littered with "lack of structure", "wandering", "starts well then meanders".

examples_expected.specificity: Measurable brand metrics with real data behind them — NOT a list of strong brand names, which the examiners explicitly rejected
examples_expected.quote: There were many answers with no factual evidence; this is a commercial paper and it is simply not possible to answer successfully without detailed analysis and real life examples.

scope_traps.trap: Reading the question as "which wine brands are strong?" and listing them, rather than "what measurements demonstrate strength?"
scope_traps.quote: All too often this just became a list of strong brands - not at all what the question was looking for.

performance_note: "A popular question, and seemingly fairly straightforward, but in fact this received the lowest average mark and the lowest pass rate."
extraction_notes: examples_expected.quote is from the Paper 4 paper-level General Comments; this question's own commentary demands metrics and explicitly penalises a list of brands, so a grader should read "examples" here as quantified evidence, not named brands. "quantifiable" is treated as a required element rather than a definitions_required entry because the report says it was the key word, not that candidates had to define it.
